stem: A pipeline at Stonebridge Mutual initializes one configuration for three environments. The bucket name and state key differ per environment, and credentials come from the runner. No secrets may reach the repository. What is the right setup?

choices.text: Hardcode the credentials in the backend block for each environment; only `-backend-config` values are copied into plan files, so hardcoded ones stay private
Skip the backend block altogether and supply the bucket name only on the `terraform init` command line
Pass the values with `-backend-config` and commit the resulting `.terraform` directory so every environment's runner reuses the same settings
Keep an empty backend block naming the type, pass differing values with `-backend-config`, and give credentials through environment variables

rationale: A partial configuration leaves arguments out of the block, which still has to exist at minimum as an empty block that names the backend type; the rest arrive through `-backend-config` (a file or key and value pairs) at init. Environment variables are the recommended way to supply credentials. Hardcoded values and `-backend-config` values both end up in the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files, so hardcoding is not private. The `.terraform` directory can hold sensitive credentials and should not be committed. Omitting the block entirely fails because Terraform needs the type declared.
